text: Hello everyone and welcome back to Systems Engineering Hub.
Today we are dissecting event-driven architecture using Rust.
At 2 minutes in, we configure the multi-threaded Tokio runtime for minimal context switching.
By pinning worker threads to specific CPU cores, cache locality improves by 40%.
Next at 6 minutes 40 seconds, let's examine zero-copy buffer pooling.
Using bytes crate slicing eliminates heap reallocations across network frame boundaries.
Looking at benchmarks against our Go baseline, Rust shows a 3x throughput gain under p99 latency.
To conclude, choosing zero-copy primitives is essential when servicing over 100k requests per second.
